summary: Savannah River entrance light on Tybee Island: the brick tower of 1867 stands on a site marked since 1736 and is now a museum.

access.note: Ticketed visits on posted hours; closed Tuesdays; the lighthouse and catwalk may close for weather.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1736 tower was a daymark (LighthouseFriends); the NRHP calls it the first recorded lighthouse without saying it was lit, and Wikipedia says the first two towers were never lit. The record's 1736 first_lit is therefore not supported; the first lighting the sources date firmly is 1 October 1867 for the present tower.

The Morning News of 10 June 1889 says the tower was blown up by Confederate forces as they left; the NRHP nomination says the Montgomery Guards burned it and only partially destroyed it. The 1889 feature is a newspaper account and the nomination is a later survey; neither is confirmed by a third source, and the story gives both.

notes_for_editor: KEEPERS: roster generated by roster.py --json for the rear tower (181 lines, place slug tybee-island-range-rear, matched by the candidate list) and the front beacon (4 lines, tybee-island-range-front); roles are roster.py's normalisation. The USLHS 'Contractor' heading (Winslow Lewis, no dates) is not counted as a keeper. Coast Guard lines (about 1950 to 1971) are kept as printed with position not stated; the story names none of them. ROSTER CAVEAT: Mrs. Francis Sickel and Mary L. Cohen etc. are spelled as printed. DISPUTES NOT SETTLED: height 145 ft (NRHP) vs 154 ft total (LighthouseFriends, and Wikipedia); first-order (NRHP) vs second-order (LighthouseFriends) lens in 1857; fire year 1862 (NRHP) vs 1861 (LighthouseFriends); base dated 1791 (NRHP) vs third tower 1773 (LighthouseFriends). AUTOMATION: the record and Wikipedia give 1972; no source read gives that year, so it is left out. Wikipedia is used for leads only and is not cited. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: facts and short quotations only. NEWSPAPERS: one Chronicling America search (Tybee light, lighthouse, Georgia, 1860-1925) returned 20 hits; two pages were read: The Morning News (Savannah) of 10 June 1889 p. 8 (keepers' routine) and 6 June 1897 p. 6 (feature on the tower; only its climb sentence is used). The 1889 names are linked to the roster by post and year only (Keeper Jacobs = Peter Jacob; Peter Rasmusson; John L. Evans = John Simmons Evans); the spellings differ. The 1889 'blown up' account conflicts with the nomination's partial burning. The 1897 feature's history passages are vague and partly speculative, so they are not used. Newspaper OCR is poor; quotes are taken from the OCR as printed. LHB 1901 'heavy guns' statement is taken from LighthouseFriends because that volume has no OCR page index. Dates: the task brief says today is 2026-10-22, but the system clock reads 2026-10-27; accessed dates use 2026-10-27. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-22: 1736 tower material is now stated as disputed (LighthouseFriends wooden, NRHP brickwork and cedar piles). Roster count corrected to 180 named lines (the contractor line is not counted). The living Coast Guard name in the roster example was removed from the prose. The 1889 newspaper says Peter Jacobs had been at his post six years; the roster starts him as first assistant in 1884 and head keeper in 1888; the story states this. The 1889 'abandoned the bland' is an OCR error for island. LighthouseFriends prose is paraphrased; quotations kept are NRHP, Board report, Bulletin, roster and newspaper wording.
